top_choice_rationale: P002 (Katori and Ye, optical lattice clock) is the most mature and most cleanly attributed achievement on the slate: the magic-wavelength lattice is a distinct concept, Ye's work showed the 1e-18 performance, and the atomic-structure inputs (polarizabilities, blackbody shifts) have been checked independently across laboratories and species. The two-name credit needs no forced exclusions among the credited names, though the citation must name the lattice concept so it stays apart from the 2005 and 2012 prizes. P001 is second because the discovery is real and reproduced, but disorder sensitivity, the open pairing mechanism and the Lopes dos Santos precursor make it less settled. P003 is third because its credit chain (Zoller versus Cirac, Jaksch outside the list) is unresolved. No award is last because every proposal rests on substantial, reproduced physics.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my documented collaborators (Lindgren group, L'Huillier and Lund, Keller at ETH, Schuch, Dahlstrom, Argenti, Indelicato) are not among the credited names in P001, P002 or P003. I note only disciplinary closeness to optical-clock atomic structure as a possible bias.
